posts.title: Signal+TLS over MPC for anonymous notification of ICE activity
posts.description: We describe AnonAlert, a system for delivering notifications in an anonymous way. People Over Papers (a.k.a. POP or iceout.org) is a website for tracking ICE activity. Users can submit reports, which then get validated by moderators and displayed on a map. Users can also sign up for notifications of activity in their area. Given the level of repression by the US government there is reason for users of POP to be concerned about their privacy: a database of people (their IP, their approximate location, etc.) interested in tracking ICE activity could be a useful starting point for more generally targeted repression.

posts.title: How to evaluate blueprints for socialism
posts.description: Beggs, Burgis, and Sunkar’s recent book “The Blueprint: How Socialism Can Work in the Real World” puts forward a concrete proposal for what they call socialism. It is a set of institutions and social practices that they believe would yield a society that is both (a) desirable – i.e., would ameliorate the issues of our current world 1 – and (b) viable, that is, able to reproduce itself over time. They do not attempt to argue its “feasibility”, that we could actually get there from where we are now.

posts.title: Primitive accumulation produces a surplus population
posts.description: This post is about a formalization of an simple argument Jasper Bernes explained to me yesterday which proves that primitive accumulation produces a surplus population. Marx in Capital explains surplus population as resulting from the introduction of labor saving technology, which reduces the need for workers (i.e., “automation”.) But, there is an additional source of surplus population, which is primitive accumulation: people formerly living off the land by a non-capitalist mode of production, who are dispossessed.
